newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close higher on rate cut hopes.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close higher on rate cut hopes.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Thursday on expectations of a cut in interest rates at the end of the month and lower yields on CPI-linked bonds, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct to 106.09
Volume including Makams was 199 million shekels.
"The market rose across the board today, mainly on expectations that the central bank will lower interest rates at the end of the month," said a trader.
"The main rises were in long-term CPI-linked bonds, which is an indication of an expectation of lower interest rates," he said.
He added that demand for unlinked bonds was up also because inflation in the coming months is expected to be low.
But expectations of falling yields also affected trading on Thursday.

"Demand for long term CPI-linked bonds was high today, on expectations that yields on CPI-linked bonds will fall below four percent," said Eyal Segal of United Mizrahi Bank. "Long term bonds gain the most when yields fall," he said.
Yields of long-term CPI-linked bonds are at 4.1 to 4.2 percent, while yields on short-term CPI-linked bonds float between 4.1 to 4.4 percent, he said.

Some traders are forecasting a fall in bond yields because of a tighter supply of bonds. Three months of budget surpluses and increased privatisation revenues have enabled the government to raise less debt, traders said.
The price of dollar-linked bonds rose on Thursday because of a strengthening of the dollar worldwide, traders said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
- Shoshanna Solomon, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233 SAS DJS
